claims.text: Grothman's 2024 'inside and outside of the SCIF' framing is in tension with Luna's 2025 statement that DoD told committee staff Oversight members were not eligible to be read in on the relevant special access programs without HASC/HAC-D approval. Either the SCIF sessions did not reach the SAPs at issue, or the two chairs were describing different access. Reasoning: both statements are on the record of the same committee thirteen months apart and cannot both describe complete access to the same material.

label: Glenn S. Grothman
narrative: Grothman gavelled in the first UAP hearing of the modern disclosure era. As Chairman of the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs he presided on 26 July 2023, waived six non-members onto the panel - Burchett, Luna, Gaetz, Burlison, Ocasio-Cortez and Ogles - swore the witnesses, and opened by saying that lack of transparency on UAP 'has fueled wild speculation and debate for decades, eroding public trust in the very institutions that are meant to serve and protect them.' He co-chaired the 13 November 2024 joint hearing with Mace and co-led H.R. 6967 with Garcia. His 2024 opening statement is also the board's cleanest artifact of the containment position from inside the disclosure caucus: he stated that no agency had been able to substantiate Grusch's claims 'despite our Committee Members endlessly questioning these agencies inside and outside of the SCIF.' Read against Luna's 2025 disclosure that Oversight members could not be read in on the relevant SAPs at all without HASC and HAC-D approval, the two statements do not describe the same access - which is exactly the seam the coverup strand exists to record.
